_comment: T6.10 (DOC-004, DOC-006): the 'For nerds' page. site/build.py checks this file against the repo: every crate under crates/ must be here and nothing else, dependency arrows come from the crates' Cargo.toml files (not from this file), every ADR and requirement ID must exist in spec/, every 'code' path must exist, and every stack entry with a 'crate' must be a real dependency.

telltale-net.summary: Listeners: UDP worker threads, TCP, DNS over TLS and HTTPS, PROXY protocol v2.
telltale-net.detail: One UDP socket per worker thread and listen address (SO_REUSEPORT), so cores never contend for a socket. TCP, DoT and DoH (HTTP/2) run as tokio tasks and call the same synchronous handler, so every transport behaves the same. Certificates reload without a restart; DoT SNI and the DoH path can carry a client ID. This is the only crate allowed to use unsafe (socket options and syscalls), each use with a SAFETY note.

telltale-proto.summary: Zero-copy DNS wire parser and writer for the hot path.
telltale-proto.detail: Reads the header, question and EDNS straight from the packet buffer without allocating, fingerprints the name (xxh3) for the cache and filter, and writes answers in place: blocked answers, error answers with extended DNS errors, and TTL patches. Anything it can't parse becomes FORMERR or a drop, never a panic.
telltale-proto.budget: Reading a question and fingerprinting it: about 53 ns.

telltale-policy.summary: Who is asking, which groups they're in, and the early checks.
telltale-policy.detail: Identifies the client by address, MAC (from EDNS or the neighbour table), or client ID; resolves its groups (devices and network groups); applies allowed networks, the per-client token-bucket rate limit, pauses, special-use names, and answers local names. The tables are read-mostly behind ArcSwap, so lookups never take a lock.

telltale-filter.summary: Blocklists: fetch, parse, compile into a snapshot, and match.
telltale-filter.detail: Downloads lists with ETag and If-Modified-Since, parses hosts files, AdBlock syntax and Pi-hole regexes, and compiles everything off the DNS path into one compact snapshot: FSTs of names plus a regex DFA, with a hash index for query time. A new snapshot replaces the old one atomically. Every decision keeps its list and line, which is what 'Why?' and explain show.
telltale-filter.budget: About 9 bytes per blocked name; a lookup takes under a microsecond.

telltale-cache.summary: Sharded S3-FIFO cache of finished wire responses.
telltale-cache.detail: Keeps each upstream reply as bytes plus the offsets of its TTLs, so a hit is a copy and a few small writes (the client's ID, case, and the aged TTLs). Negative answers and SERVFAIL are cached too. Concurrent misses for one name share one upstream request (singleflight); popular names are prefetched before they expire, expired answers can be served while upstreams are down, and the cache can be saved across restarts.
telltale-cache.budget: Copy and patch a cached answer: about 5 ns; a full cache hit end to end: about 153 ns.

telltale-upstream.summary: Upstream servers: transports, groups, strategies, hedging, breakers, DNSSEC.
telltale-upstream.detail: Plain DNS, DoT and DoH upstreams with connection pools and bootstrap addresses; groups with failover, round-robin, weighted, fastest, or parallel strategies; routes that send a domain (optionally only for some groups) to a chosen server. A slow server is hedged after about 3x its usual time and a failing one is benched by a circuit breaker. DNSSEC validation uses hickory's validator over the same upstream groups.

telltale-recursor.summary: Reserved for full recursive resolution; empty today.
telltale-recursor.detail: A placeholder for iterative resolution from the root (planned after 1.0). DNSSEC validation, which the plan once put here, lives in telltale-upstream instead (ADR-060).

telltale-telemetry.summary: QueryEvents, lock-free rings, the aggregator, rollups, and Prometheus.
telltale-telemetry.detail: Every answer leaves a fixed-size QueryEvent in its worker's single-producer ring; the hot path never waits on telemetry, and a full ring drops and counts. One aggregator thread turns events into counters, top-K lists, HDR latency histograms, per-device baselines for anomaly detection, the live tail, and the query log.

telltale-store.summary: The columnar query-log store and SQLite state.
telltale-store.detail: The query log is one file per hour: 19 columns in zstd-compressed blocks with a name dictionary and a per-hour name filter, so a search skips hours and columns it doesn't need. SQLite (WAL) holds users, tokens, the hash-chained audit log, rollups, and devices and names made in the UI.

telltale-api.summary: The REST API, sign-in, OpenAPI, live tail, MCP, and the embedded UI.
telltale-api.detail: axum on its own listener (8053 by default). Browser sessions with CSRF tokens, scoped API and agent tokens, opt-in HTTP Basic for scrapers, and OIDC; three roles. The OpenAPI document is generated from the code (utoipa). Server-Sent Events stream the live tail, and POST /mcp serves read-only MCP tools that call the same routes with the caller's rights. The Svelte UI is built into the binary.

telltale-cluster.summary: Membership, PKI, replication, failover, and federation over mTLS.
telltale-cluster.detail: Every node has a certificate from the cluster CA; nodes talk over one HTTP/2 mTLS channel carrying protobuf frames (hello, heartbeats with RTT and config version, manifests, key shares, votes). The primary publishes signed manifests of content-addressed blobs; replicas fetch only what changed and keep answering from their last copy. Failover is manual or elected with fencing epochs; the CA can be rotated without downtime.

telltale-config.summary: The TOML schema, validation, defaults, and shared vs node-local sections.
telltale-config.detail: One serde schema for every setting, with errors that point at the exact key. It also prints the JSON Schema that the configuration reference on this site is built from, and decides which sections are shared across a cluster and which stay on each node.

telltale-git.summary: Reads one file at a ref from a Git server (smart-HTTP v2), no Git binary.
telltale-git.detail: A small client for the Git smart-HTTP protocol v2: it asks for one ref, fetches only the objects for one file, inflates them, and can check commit signatures against allowed signers. This is how the cluster's configuration can come from a Git repository.

telltale.summary: The binary: wires every crate together, plus the CLI.
telltale.detail: Owns the query pipeline that calls the crates above in order, the server roles, replication and the Git source, query-log shipping, the importers (Pi-hole, Technitium), backups, self-update and the update check, the MCP stdio bridge, and every command (run, explain, lists, auth, cluster, import, backup, mcp, self-update).

pipeline.title: Receive
pipeline.summary: A worker thread reads a batch of UDP packets from its own socket, or a TCP/DoT/DoH task reads one request.

pipeline.title: Parse
pipeline.summary: Header, question and EDNS read in place. Malformed input becomes FORMERR or a drop.

pipeline.title: Early checks
pipeline.summary: Allowed networks (never an open resolver), the per-client rate limit, our own loop tag, ANY (a tiny RFC 8482 answer), and special-use names like localhost.

pipeline.title: Your names
pipeline.summary: Names on your network are answered right here, before the cache or any upstream.

pipeline.title: Who's asking
pipeline.summary: The client by address, MAC, or client ID, and its groups.

pipeline.title: Block or allow
pipeline.summary: The groups' lists decide; a block is answered immediately and records the list and line.

pipeline.title: Route
pipeline.summary: Which upstream group: a route for this domain (optionally only for some groups), else the default. Private reverse lookups stay local.

pipeline.title: Cache
pipeline.summary: A hit is copied and patched, CNAME targets are checked against the lists, and popular names are prefetched. A miss or an expired entry goes on.

pipeline.title: Ask upstream
pipeline.summary: Async: the group's strategy picks a server, a slow one is hedged, a failing one is benched. If every server fails, a stale answer is better than none.

pipeline.title: Validate
pipeline.summary: Optional DNSSEC validation; a bogus answer becomes SERVFAIL with an extended error, never a stale answer.

pipeline.title: Answer and record
pipeline.summary: The reply is cached and sent, and a QueryEvent with per-stage timings goes into the worker's ring for the aggregator.

cluster.title: Joining
cluster.summary: telltale cluster init makes a CA; a join token pins it; the joining node gets a certificate. Only the primary's port has to be reachable.

cluster.title: Replication
cluster.summary: The primary signs a manifest of BLAKE3-addressed blobs (config, compiled lists). Replicas fetch the blobs they lack, verify, and swap atomically.

cluster.title: DNS independence
cluster.summary: Every node answers from its last applied snapshot, from disk at cold start, whatever the cluster's state.

cluster.title: Failover
cluster.summary: Manual promote, or elected with three or more voters (a witness counts). Epochs fence an old primary out.

cluster.title: One management plane
cluster.summary: Any node's UI reads the whole cluster (federated queries) and forwards changes to the primary, vouching for the user over mTLS.

cluster.title: Kubernetes pods
cluster.summary: Resolver pods join with a shared bootstrap secret, ship their query log to the controller, and are swept when they disappear.

cluster.title: Upgrades and keys
cluster.summary: Versions N and N-1 interoperate; certificates renew over the channel; the CA rotates in three member-gated phases.

agents.title: Agent tokens
agents.summary: Scoped (analytics:read, config:write:clients, ops:pause, ...), deny by default per route, a reason header on every change, per-token rate limits, and a kill switch.

agents.title: MCP server
agents.summary: POST /mcp on every node, plus telltale mcp --stdio for desktop clients. Tools call the REST routes in-process with the caller's credentials, so scopes apply inside tools too. Resources (cluster status, the configuration, a daily summary) and prompts for common questions. Write tools make plans from the REST dry run; apply_plan replays them with If-Match, after an operator's approval when required.

items.name: tokio
items.why: Async runtime for TCP, TLS, HTTP and upstream work; the UDP fast path runs on its own threads.

items.name: socket2
items.why: SO_REUSEPORT and other socket options for one socket per worker.

items.name: rustls
items.why: TLS for DoT, DoH, upstreams and the cluster channel, without OpenSSL.

items.name: hyper / h2
items.why: HTTP/2 for DoH and the cluster channel.

items.name: mimalloc
items.why: A fast allocator for the control plane; the hot path barely allocates.

items.name: arc-swap
items.why: Readers of the snapshot and policy tables never lock; a swap is one pointer store.

items.name: fst
items.why: Finite-state transducers: millions of blocked names in a few bytes each.

items.name: regex-automata
items.why: Compiles every regex rule into one DFA, checked once per name.

items.name: xxhash-rust (xxh3)
items.why: Name fingerprints for the cache key and the snapshot's hash index.

items.name: hickory-net
items.why: DNSSEC chain-of-trust validation: the long tail, not the hot path.

items.name: idna
items.why: Unicode domain names in lists, turned into their wire form.

items.name: rtrb
items.why: Wait-free single-producer rings from each worker to the aggregator.

items.name: hdrhistogram
items.why: Latency percentiles with fixed memory.

items.name: zstd
items.why: Compresses query-log blocks, blobs on the wire, and backups.

items.name: rusqlite (bundled SQLite)
items.why: Users, tokens, audit log, rollups; one file, WAL mode.

items.name: blake3
items.why: Content addresses for snapshot blobs and backup checksums.

items.name: axum
items.why: The REST API and the MCP endpoint.

items.name: utoipa
items.why: OpenAPI generated from the handlers, so the docs and UI types can't drift.

items.name: argon2 + totp-rs
items.why: Password hashing and authenticator-app codes.

items.name: openidconnect
items.why: Sign-in with Keycloak, Authentik, or any OIDC provider.

items.name: rcgen + x509-parser
items.why: The cluster CA and node certificates.

items.name: prost
items.why: Protobuf frames on the cluster channel, versioned for N/N-1.

items.name: minisign-verify
items.why: Checks release signatures in self-update and the update check.

items.name: rust-embed
items.why: Builds the UI into the binary.

items.name: clap
items.why: The command line.

items.name: Svelte 5 + Vite
items.why: A small, compiled UI; the bundle budget is 400 KiB gzipped.

items.name: uPlot
items.why: Fast canvas charts with a table view for each.

items.name: openapi-typescript
items.why: TypeScript types generated from the API's OpenAPI document.

items.name: Playwright
items.why: End-to-end tests against a real server, and the screenshots on this site.

items.name: GitHub Actions
items.why: Clippy, tests, fuzzing, kind clusters, a Pi-hole and Technitium import, OIDC against Keycloak and Authentik, upgrade tests.

items.name: cargo-deny
items.why: License and advisory checks on every dependency (no copyleft code).

items.name: cargo-fuzz
items.why: Fuzzes the query and response parsers, list parsing, and query-log segments.

items.name: musl + FROM scratch
items.why: A static binary in an image of about 9 MiB for amd64, arm64 and armv7.

items.name: Helm (OCI)
items.why: The chart, published to ghcr.io on every build.

items.name: minisign
items.why: Signed release binaries and a signed release index.

formats.name: Filter snapshot
formats.summary: Per-group FSTs of names, a regex DFA, rule metadata (list and line), and a hash index; content-addressed blobs listed in a manifest.

formats.name: Cluster manifest
formats.summary: Version, epoch, config hash, blob hashes and CA bundle, signed by the primary; JSON over the mTLS channel.

formats.name: Query-log segment (.seg)
formats.summary: One file per hour: a header, a name dictionary and name filter, then zstd blocks of 19 columns, each block checksummed.

formats.name: QueryEvent
formats.summary: A fixed-size record per answer with per-stage timings in microseconds, written into byte rings.

formats.name: Backup (.ttbk)
formats.summary: A zstd-compressed tar with a manifest of BLAKE3 checksums, written owner-only; restore verifies everything first.

formats.name: Release index (releases.json)
formats.summary: Every published build per channel, signed with minisign; nodes trust it only after checking the signature.
